latest_findings.claim: The N=64 reference arm (d_model=128, m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 1, seed 24, 6000 steps) beats its force control: force R2 = 0.8339 at layer 1 vs control 0.60961 (margin 0.224, headroom-normalised 0.57). accel_step is decoded better: R2 = 0.97248 at layer 4 vs control 0.79073 (margin 0.182, normalised 0.87). The predicted N=64 minus N=128 force gap could not be computed, because the paired N=128 run (run-20261016-072048-0756) is still running.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This rests on one completed run at full completion (6000/6000 steps, val_mse_ratio 0.0029). It satisfies only the first condition of expected_if_true (N=64 force margin >= 0.1). The primary test, a force gap >= 0.04 at the best-margin layer and at layer 1, is not computed until the N=128 seed-24 arm finishes, so the hypothesis can be neither supported nor refuted yet. The accel_step sub-clause cannot be scored either: N=64 accel_step peaks at layer 4, not layer 1, and there are no N=128 values. Force was still rising at step 6000 (about +0.002 R2 per 500 steps from step 4500), while accel_step had levelled off. The endpoint therefore depends on the 6000-step schedule, and the paired arm must be read at the same horizon and at layer 1. If the N=128 final layer-1 force R2 is <= 0.7939, the verdict becomes supported. If it is >= 0.8139, it becomes refuted. Anything in between is inconclusive. Even then, this is a single seed on data_seed 1.

latest_findings.claim: At matched 24000-step horizon (N=64, seed 23, m2 fixed, data_seed 0, d_model=64), final layer-1 force R2 = 0.75294 vs control 0.54241 (margin 0.211, best layer 1). That is 0.0401 above the same-layer N=128 seed-23 24000-step value of 0.71286 (run-20261014-070746-d284), right at the 0.04 bar. The pre-registered horizon check fails: at step 12000 layer-1 force is about 0.752 (control plus margin 0.210; trajectory field 0.756), 0.037-0.041 below the 12000-step run's endpoint of 0.7935 (run-20261014-043150-2de3). accel_step is unchanged: R2 0.941 at layer 4 vs control 0.744, headroom-normalised margin 0.77, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.85].
latest_findings.confidence_note: The run completed all 24000 steps with no early stop. The headline gap only just clears 0.04 (0.0401), and it does so only because 0.71286 + 0.04 = 0.75286 is slightly below the rounded 0.753 threshold. The pre-registered horizon check (step-12000 layer-1 within 0.03 of 0.7935) fails by about 0.007-0.011, so under the stated rules this result is horizon-confounded. The trajectory is non-monotone. Layer-1 force peaks at about 0.773 at steps 5000-6000 (margin 0.231), drifts down to about 0.750 by step 13000, then recovers only slightly to 0.753. The 24000-step endpoint is therefore about 0.04 below the 12000-step endpoint (0.7935), the same pattern as seed 22 (0.804 vs 0.840). That suggests endpoint force is set by the lr schedule shape rather than by total training. At roughly matched loss (step 14000, val_mse_ratio 0.0048, vs N=128's 0.0052) layer-1 force is about 0.750, a gap of about 0.037, again on the bar. This is a single seed. Intermediate layer-1 values assume the control is fixed across checkpoints, i.e. final control 0.54241 plus trajectory margin. What would change the verdict: a 12000-vs-24000 comparison at matched schedule fraction showing the two N=64 runs agree within 0.03 (the horizon check would then be satisfied), plus a second seed whose matched-horizon same-layer gap clears 0.04 with room to spare.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 with m2 fixed (seed 24, data_seed 0, 6000 steps), N=128 force peaks at layer 1 with trained R2 0.78436 against a control of 0.63366 (margin 0.151). The paired N=64 arm also peaks at layer 1 and ends at about 0.842 (trajectory value, margin 0.205), so the same-layer N=64 minus N=128 gap is about 0.058. That clears the 0.04 bar, and nearly all of it is in trained R2: the controls are about 0.637 vs 0.634. accel_step is essentially unchanged across the two arms: here layer-4 R2 is 0.96197 vs control 0.75519, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.845, which falls inside [0.60, 0.88]. The N=64 arm reads about 0.966 on its trajectory.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is one seed, and the N=64 reference (run-20261016-055050-9600, paired arm exp-20261016-034512-611f) is only available as rounded trajectory values. Its trajectory R2 field may be the max over layers rather than the layer-1 value, so the gap of about 0.058 could be off by about 0.01. The gap is only measured at matched step, not matched loss. Across checkpoints it stays at about 0.058-0.064 from step 1000 to step 6000, and both arms' force margins are still rising by about 0.002-0.004 per 500 steps. The seed-24 gap of about 0.058 falls between seed 22 (0.108) and seed 23 (0.045) at d128, so it is consistent with a persistent deficit at d128 and adds a third seed in that direction. The verdict would change in either of two cases: the unrounded N=64 layer-1 probes_final R2 comes out below 0.8244, or a reading at matched val_mse_ratio (N=128 ends at 0.015) puts the gap below 0.04. A seed-24 d64 pair is still needed before this seed can say anything about width-driven shrinkage.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=128 (m2=0.5, data_seed 0, e<=0.5, 6000 steps, seed 24), N=64 force beats its control at layer 1: R2 0.84173 vs control 0.63702, margin 0.205. The paired N=128 arm (run-20261016-060747-3fef) also has force best at layer 1, with step-6000 trajectory R2 0.784 (margin 0.151), so the same-layer layer-1 N=64 minus N=128 trained force R2 gap is about 0.058, above the 0.04 bar. The gap stays at 0.054-0.064 at every checkpoint from step 500 to 6000. accel_step is the same in both arms (layer 4, R2 0.96638 vs about 0.962). This arm's accel_step headroom-normalised margin is 0.861 (control 0.75813), inside the predicted [0.60, 0.88], and its accel_step margin (0.208) is about the same as its force margin (0.205).
latest_findings.confidence_note: There is one seed on one dataset, and this experiment has only one run. The N=128 value comes from the paired arm's rounded trajectory field (its 4th field may be max-over-layers R2 rather than the best-margin-layer R2, see q-20261013-075749-57bb), not from its unrounded probes_final, so the gap of about 0.058 is approximate to about ±0.005. That uncertainty cannot push it below 0.04. The comparison is at matched step and horizon, not matched val_mse_ratio. N=64 reaches val_mse_ratio 0.0035, and the N=128 loss trajectory is not shown here. Both arms are still gaining force at step 6000 (N=128 about +0.003-0.004 per 500 steps, N=64 about +0.002), so the gap may narrow slowly with longer training. Seed 24's d128 gap (0.058) sits between seeds 22 (0.108) and 23 (0.045), so all three d128 seeds now clear 0.04. No d64 run of seed 24 exists, so this run says nothing about how much width shrinks the gap for this seed. The verdict would change if the N=128 probes_final layer-1 R2 came out at 0.80 or above, if a matched-loss read put the gap below 0.04, or if more seeds on data_seed 1 at d128 fell below 0.02.

latest_findings.claim: At d_model=256 (N=64, m2 fixed, seed 22, 6000 steps), final force R2 at the best-margin layer (layer 1) is 0.82857 against a control of 0.60495 (margin 0.224 ≥ 0.1). That is within 0.002 of the d_model=128 value (0.82669, layer 4) and within 0.005 of the d_model=64 value (0.8235, layer 1), so N=64 force at its best-margin layer does not rise with width. accel_step is also best at layer 1 with R2 0.92803 against a control of 0.74143, a headroom-normalised margin of 0.72. Distance (R2 0.991) and energy (R2 0.976) are decoded almost perfectly but fail the bar only because their d256 controls are 0.895 and 0.927. Against the paired d256 N=128 arm (run-20261016-042805-cfe4, force best layer 1), the gap can only be estimated from trajectory fields. The best-margin-layer estimate is about 0.03 (0.829 vs about 0.795). The max-over-layers estimate is about 0.07 (0.867 vs 0.795). Both are below the d64 gap of 0.143 and the d128 gap of 0.108.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is one seed (22) on one dataset, and the pre-registered criterion is met. Three things limit confidence. (1) The three widths are compared at different layers: d64 at layer 1, d128 at layer 4, d256 at layer 1. (2) The trajectory's max-over-layers force R2 at step 6000 is 0.867, so some layer other than the best-margin layer 1 (one with a higher control) goes above the 0.86 'width still lifts force' cutoff. Read at the best layer by raw R2 instead of by margin, the result would fall on the expected-if-false side. A fixed-layer readout across d64/d128/d256 could flip the verdict. (3) The paired N=128 gap comes from trajectory fields, not probes_final, so it is an estimate and is not used as evidence here. The verdict would change if per-layer probes_final showed d256 force at some fixed layer at least 0.03 above the same layer at d128, or if a second seed (for example seed 23) moved by more than 0.03. Force was still rising slowly at step 6000 (+0.002 margin from 4500 to 6000).

config.expected_if_false: N=128 trained force R2 is within 0.02 of the same-seed N=64 value at the best-margin layer. A gap in (0.02, 0.04) is inconclusive.
config.expected_if_true: N=128 trained force R2 is at least 0.04 below the same-seed d_model=128 N=64 value at the best-margin layer, and also at layer 1 if both arms list it. The accel_step normalised-margin difference is reported separately.
config.hypothesis: Test arm for a third-seed d_model=128 width replication on data_seed 1. Setup: m2 fixed at 0.5, e in [0, 0.5], 4 layers, d_model=128, best-of-3 controls, seed 24, N=128, 6000 steps. Prediction: the N=128 force deficit persists at twice the width, so final trained force R2 is at least 0.04 below the same seed's d_model=128 N=64 value from the paired arm proposed this cycle. All values come from probes_final, unrounded. The primary gap is computed at the best-margin layer, with layers reported and cross-layer pairs flagged. A layer-1 same-layer gap is also reported wherever both arms list layer 1. Within-run values are read only as same-layer control plus margin, never from the max-over-layers trajectory field. A secondary clause compares the headroom-normalised accel_step margin across arms at the same layer and is scored separately from the force verdict. Both arms' run IDs are cited as evidence. If the paired run is unavailable, the gap is reported as not computed.
